claims.statement: createRoutes in packages/server/src/routes/index.ts builds the API surface from a declared RouteMount[] table ({ prefix, middleware, router }) registered by mountRoutes, which records each layer's prefix and an authenticated flag (derived from the requiresAuth brand on mount middleware) in a WeakMap, because Express 5 hides mount prefixes in matcher closures; the same table feeds both runtime mounting and the route inventory/openapi.json.

Express registration order is load-bearing in the mount table: /swarms/spawns (requireAuthOrSpawnToken) and /swarm-v2/social-runtime (empty middleware, signed runtime callbacks, no user JWT) must precede /swarms and /swarm-v2, and diff routes mount at '/' with no mount-level guard because each handler authenticates itself and a '/' guard would intercept later public routes such as the Telegram webhook.

createRoutes throws AUTH_MIDDLEWARE_REQUIRED at construction when authService or the auth middleware is missing, and applies security headers, a 1 MB request-body cap (limitBodySize(1_000_000), 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE), and a global 300 req/min per-IP express-rate-limit limiter to the whole /api router.

Nearly all /api prefixes mount requireAuth; the exceptions are /auth (empty middleware, public login), /swarms/spawns (requireAuthOrSpawnToken admits either a user JWT or scoped X-Spawn-Token, while POST /spawns/root still requires write:swarm_action so token-only children cannot create roots), /swarm-v2/social-runtime (empty middleware, signed runtime callbacks), /api/health (empty middleware with self-authenticating deep/metrics variants), /telegram (empty middleware, secret webhook), /gym-worker and /host-agent (empty middleware but per-host HMAC token validation, minting requires manage:tokens), and the public GET /api/version direct route.

GET /api/openapi.json is requireAuth-guarded (with its own 100 per 15 min limiter) and lazily builds and caches an OpenAPI 3.1 skeleton from the live router stack via collectRoutes + buildOpenApiSpec: Express ':param' segments become '{param}' templates, authenticated operations get a bearerAuth security requirement, and the spec intentionally contains paths/methods/auth-flags only with no request/response schemas; collectRoutes fails closed by throwing on unrecorded nested routers and non-string paths.

GET /metrics is mounted outside /api and is default-off: it responds 404 unless METRICS_TOKEN is set, then requires 'Authorization: Bearer <METRICS_TOKEN>' compared with timingSafeEqual (plain bearer because JWT auth does not fit scrapers), is rate-limited to 300 scrapes per 15 minutes per IP, and computes all gauges per scrape directly from SQLite (plus ws-clients and process gauges) so no in-process counter state exists across restarts.

GET /health (app-level) and GET /api/health are public liveness endpoints exposing a build identity block (commit, built_commit, build_source, build_time, instance_id) via buildProvenance(); built_commit reflects the baked build and commit_matches_build is true only when the runtime commit equals the baked build commit; /api/health/deep requires read:evidence and probes database, memory, worker leases, knowledge runtime, and LiteLLM/Ollama/Qdrant, returning 503 on any error, while authenticated /api/metrics and /api/metrics/json (read:evidence) are distinct from the root /metrics scrape endpoint.

/explore serves unauthenticated, rate-limited (120 req/min per IP) public explainer pages — HTML page, llms.txt, opengraph.svg, badge.svg, sitemap.xml and robots.txt — with strict owner/repo pattern validation and 404s for unpublished repositories; /explore/leaderboard is default-off (404 unless OPENMYTHOS_LEADERBOARD_PUBLIC=true) and emits scores only for model-only governance runs, and production startup fails if DJIMITFLO_PUBLIC_ORIGIN is missing or not http/https.

The WebSocket server shares the HTTP server at path /ws; the dashboard client authenticates by offering the session token as a 'bearer.<token>' subprotocol (avoiding token leakage via logs/history/referrers) and the server's handleProtocols echoes it per RFC 6455, after which WebSocketService rejects the connection with close code 4001 for missing token, 4002 for invalid token/disabled user, or 4003 for expired token, and sends an initial system.health message on success.

WebSocket authority is continuously re-validated, not handshake-only: every send and broadcast passes through getAuthenticatedClient, which closes the socket (4003/4002) when the token has expired, the user is disabled, role/email/organization changed, or the session sid was revoked, forcing clients to rebind through a fresh connection so stale privileges are never emitted.

WebSocketService exposes audience-targeted broadcast helpers (broadcastToAuthenticated, broadcastToAdmins, broadcastToUser, broadcastTaskEvent filtered by AuthorizationService.canReadTask, debate-scoped broadcasts) and skips clients whose bufferedAmount exceeds WS_MAX_BUFFERED_AMOUNT_BYTES (default 1 MiB) rather than buffering; approvals, tasks, spawns, discussions, governance-feedback and other routes consume these helpers via their route factories.

The dashboard useWebSocket hook reconnects after 3 s only for non-auth closes while authenticated; on auth close codes it stops reconnecting, attempts exactly one refreshSession on AUTH_EXPIRED before giving up, and unwraps execution.batch envelopes to dispatch inner events individually; during SIGTERM shutdown the server closes all sockets with code 1001 plus a 5-second terminate deadline so httpServer.close() is not blocked.

The route table is verified rather than trusted: scripts/route-source-inventory.mjs statically parses createXRoutes factories and expands the mount graph from index:createRoutes at /api with a SHA-256 source fingerprint; packages/server/src/__tests__/route-inventory.test.ts instantiates the real aggregator, asserts zero drift between source declarations and the instantiated router via compareRuntimeRoutes, HTTP-probes every authenticated route anonymously requiring 401, and checks the openapi.json operation count equals inventory size; scripts/contract-inventory.mjs (assurance:contracts) cross-references routes against test evidence, flags critical unclassified routes, validates the runtime inventory fingerprint, and exits nonzero on drift.

packages/server/src/index.ts orders the whole network surface: the GitHub webhook (raw signature, before JSON parsing) first, then express.json and request logging, GET /health, the /ws WebSocketServer, GET /metrics, app.use('/api', createRoutes(...)), app.use('/explore', ...), the static dashboard with an SPA fallback that yields to /api, /ws, and /health paths, and the error handler last.

The declarative mounts table in packages/server/src/routes/index.ts (L136-L219) is the single source for both runtime mounting and the machine-readable route inventory: mountRoutes records each layer's prefix and an authenticated flag (derived from the requiresAuth brand on mount middleware) in a WeakMap keyed by the Express layer, because Express 5 hides mount prefixes inside matcher closures; besides per-prefix mounts, four routes are registered directly on the API router (public GET /api/version, requireAuth GET /api/openapi.json, and requireAuth telemetry usage/pageview routes).

Before any route matches, the API router applies in order: a 1 MB body-size cap (limitBodySize, 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE), securityHeaders, a global 300 requests/minute per-IP express-rate-limit keyed on the real client IP (trust proxy = 1), and UsageTelemetry.middleware() which records matched route patterns and page-view counts into SQLite once a minute; additional limiters are layered per prefix (/traceability 30/min, /openapi.json 100/15min, /api/health 600/min).

GET /api/openapi.json is requireAuth-guarded and lazily builds (then caches per process) an OpenAPI 3.1 skeleton from the live router stack via collectRoutes(router): prefixes are joined with route paths, Express :param segments become {param} templates, and authenticated routes get a bearerAuth security requirement; the spec is paths+methods+auth-flag only (no request/response schemas), and collectRoutes fails closed by throwing 'Route inventory incomplete' on any nested router mountRoutes did not record.

GET /metrics is mounted directly on the app (outside /api), armed only when METRICS_TOKEN is set (404 otherwise, so the endpoint is invisible); when armed it requires Authorization: Bearer <METRICS_TOKEN> compared with timingSafeEqual and is rate-limited to 300 scrapes per 15 minutes per IP via metricsRateLimiter, and all gauges (task/agent/loop/lease/approval/work-item counts by status, latest OpenMythos scores per agent, WebSocket client count, process uptime and RSS) are computed per scrape directly from SQLite so no in-process counters exist.

GET /health (app-level, public) and GET /api/health (in the mount table, public, behind a per-router 600-per-minute limiter) both report status, a timestamp, and a build identity drawn from buildProvenance(): commit (DJIMITFLO_COMMIT_SHA runtime commit), built_commit (DJIMITFLO_BUILD_COMMIT baked via Docker build args), build_source, build_time, instance_id, and commit_matches_build true only when built_commit is set and equals the runtime commit; /api/health/deep (requireAuth + read:evidence) probes database, heap memory, active worker leases, knowledge runtime validation, and configured LiteLLM/Ollama/Qdrant dependencies with a 2-second timeout, returning 503 when any check errors, while /api/metrics and /api/metrics/json (read:evidence) are distinct from the token-armed root /metrics.

The /api/mcp server registry feeds an HTTP bridge to sidecar MCP servers: POST /servers/refresh (requireAuth + manage:config) probes each registered sidecar's declared URL and, on first contact with a reachable server that exposes an openapi_url/openapi_path, bulk-imports its OpenAPI operations via services/mcp-openapi-catalog.syncOpenApiCatalog as mcp_tools rows, classifying GET/HEAD/OPTIONS as allowed/low and everything else as requires_approval/medium, capped at MAX_OPERATIONS = 100 operations per spec.

The WebSocket server shares the HTTP server at path /ws; the dashboard's useWebSocket hook sends the session token as a bearer.<token> subprotocol (not a query string, to avoid leaking into access logs/browser history/referrer headers), and the server's handleProtocols callback echoes the offered bearer.* protocol back to satisfy RFC 6455 §4.2.2; WebSocketService authenticates from that header (or a ?token= query fallback), closing with 4001 (missing), 4002 (invalid/disabled), or 4003 (expired).

WebSocket authentication is not handshake-only: every broadcast routes through getAuthenticatedClient, which closes the socket if the token has since expired (4003), the user was disabled or their role/email/organization changed (4002), or their session was revoked (4002), so authority changes force clients to rebind through a fresh connection and stale privileges are never used; slow consumers whose bufferedAmount exceeds WS_MAX_BUFFERED_AMOUNT_BYTES (default 1 MiB) are skipped rather than buffered.

The mount table is verified end-to-end rather than trusted: scripts/route-source-inventory.mjs statically parses every createXRoutes factory (literal router.<method> calls only), expands the mount graph from index:createRoutes at base /api (detecting cyclic mounts), and fingerprints all route/auth sources via SHA-256; the route-inventory.test.ts aggregator test instantiates the real router, asserts zero drift between source declarations and the live router (compareRuntimeRoutes), HTTP-probes every authenticated route anonymously requiring 401, and asserts the openapi.json operation count equals the inventory size; scripts/contract-inventory.mjs (assurance:contracts) cross-references declarations against test files, flags critical unclassified routes, validates the runtime artifact's source fingerprint as anti-staleness, and exits nonzero on drift.
